messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Pager: crashloop on prod-runtime-pool-7a (pod runtime-gpu-7a). Reason: repeated SIGSEGV in fused_attention.so. Crash count: 23 in last 7m. Impact: ~8% 5xx for /v1/generate, multiple customers seeing failures.

sam (oncall-sre): grabbing. which fleet/commit? any recent deploys?

maria (eng-runtime): saw a small canary deploy 20m ago with TRT fused kernels enabled (image: inference:v2.3.4-trt). No infra changes.

sam (oncall-sre): logs (tail from pod):
```
[2026-03-15T09:12:03Z] runtime: serve request model=gptx-2k seq_len=4096 backend=trt kv_cache=enabled
[2026-03-15T09:12:04Z] fused_attention.so +0x4f3a SIGSEGV (addr=0x7fffd9c0)
[2026-03-15T09:12:04Z] process exited with code 139 (segfault)
```

maria (eng-runtime): that addr looks like kernel shared memory access. hypothesis: fused attention with kv_cache on long sequences corrupting host/device pointers when using TRT path. I can try to reproduce locally with seq_len>=4096.

sam (oncall-sre): current mitigation? customers impacted? any dedicated customers pinned to this pool?

kevin (support): Support: 3 customers reported errors (2 on hosted, 1 on dedicated-reserved pool-3). They're seeing failed completions and retries. No P0 but one SaaS customer flagged they have active jobs.

maria (eng-runtime): quick mitigation: disable fused kernels for TRT on prod pool. env toggle: `REDWOOD_DISABLE_FUSED_KERNELS=1` or runtime flag `--disable-fused-attention`. I can push a hotpatch config to the pool to set that env on the runtime Deployment and restart pods (non-disruptive canary first).

sam (oncall-sre): do it. also open a rollback to inference:v2.3.3 as fallback if needed.

maria (eng-runtime): executing canary patch now:
```bash
kubectl -n runtime patch deploy runtime-gpu-pool-7a -p '{"spec": {"template": {"spec": {"containers": [{"name": "runtime", "env": [{"name": "REDWOOD_DISABLE_FUSED_KERNELS", "value": "1"}]}]}}}}'
```

deploy-bot: Canary update applied to runtime-gpu-pool-7a-deploy-idx-2. Rolling restart initiated.

sam (oncall-sre): monitoring liveness and 5xx rate.

(2m check)
kevin (support): one customer confirmed fewer errors after retrying. Support reaching out to the dedicated customer to schedule low-risk failover if still affected.

maria (eng-runtime): reproducer steps for upstream:
- start container with image inference:v2.3.4-trt
- run synthetic request with seq_len=4096 and kv_cache on
- observe segfault in fused_attention.so after ~10-20 requests

Quick log from local repro:
```
# gdb backtrace snippet
#0  0x00007f8b9c5c4f3a in fused_attention::compute(...) at fused_attention.cu:823
#1  0x0000560c3a2b1f9c in runtime::execute_kernel(...)
#2  0x0000560c3a2b3a11 in runtime::handle_request(...)
```
This points at index calculation in fused kernel. suspect out-of-bounds under certain sequence windows.

maria (eng-runtime): planned remediation: 1) disable fused kernels as rollout (done) 2) backport bounds-check fix to fused_attention.cu 3) run extended fuzz on seq_len distribution and TRTEngine. I'll open PR and mark for hotfix.

sam (oncall-sre): good. for customer-facing scope, propose: keep fused kernels disabled for prod pools for 24h while patch lands, route heavy long-seq workloads to a safe model variant that uses standard attention kernels (vllm-safe-2048) or smaller seq_len. Can we create a routing rule?

jen (platform): I can add a temporary routing rule in traffic-router: add policy to redirect requests with header `x-client-max-seqlen>=3072` to model alias `gptx-2k-safe` which uses non-fused runtime. Applying now to prod route but only 10% of traffic for gradual shift.

deploy-bot: Routing rule applied: header-match redirect -> gptx-2k-safe (10% traffic).

sam (oncall-sre): awesome. monitoring: 5xx dropped from 8% -> 1.2% over 8m.

kevin (support): notifying customers: sending status update: saying we identified runtime fused-kernel segfault on TRT path, temporary mitigations applied (disable fused kernels + targeted routing). ETA for full fix: 24-36 hours. Kevin to coordinate dedicated-customer failover if still seeing errors.

maria (eng-runtime): creating GitHub issue and PR: `fix/fused-attn-bounds-check-hotfix` and will target a release branch cut. PR will include regression test harness (seq_len fuzzing).

sam (oncall-sre): any resources needed from infra? GPU node drains?

jen (platform): we should avoid mass drains. the restart with env toggle is fine. if we see node flaps, we might cordon one node and repro isolated to hardware. For dedicated customer, we can provision a fallback pool with inference:v2.3.3 (non-TRT) if they need immediate guaranteed stability.

maria (eng-runtime): PR opened: https://git.redwood/inference/pulls/1248. Label: incident/segfault-trt. adding test matrix to CI.

sam (oncall-sre): handoff: I've mitigated impact (fused kernels disabled, routing rule applied), monitoring in steady state. I'm handing to jen for next shift in 30m. Pending: PR review + backport + redeploy canary for patch.

jen (platform): taking over. summary for next oncall:
- system: segfaults in fused_attention.so on TRT image 2.3.4 with kv_cache and long seqs
- mitigations applied: REDWOOD_DISABLE_FUSED_KERNELS=1 on prod pool, routing rule for long sequences to safe model, canary restarts done
- impact: short spike of 5xx (~8%) now down to ~1% ; 3 customers had reports (support notified)
- next actions: merge hotfix, backport to release branch, schedule controlled rollout and canary to prod, consider a small traffic hold for 24h

kevin (support): I'll follow up with customers and post an incident update to status.redwood.com with the mitigation steps and ETA for full fix.

jen (platform): noted. I'll coordinate the backport + deploy window with eng-runtime and infra owners. tagging @maria for release steps.

maria (eng-runtime): thanks — will prioritize the backport PR and add extended integration test. I'll ping when merge-ready.

sam (oncall-sre): leaving the channel, paging out to jen (next oncall). If anything spikes, re-pager.

incident-bot: Incident updated: severity=major, status=mitigated, assigned=jen (platform). Links: runbook/segfault-trt, PR 1248.
